localChanges: chore: update core-city, core-game, core-save-game, library-unit, civ1-unit, civ1-city and civ1-wonder

log: trade-routes yield rule (Priority 500, after worked tiles and before corruption): each route adds (partner's base trade + the city's trade so far + 4) / 8, or / 16 for a partner with the same owner, in route order; the yield's provider is the partner's id. Corruption is then worked out on the total. remove-trade-routes clears a destroyed city's routes and the routes to it (civ-clone/web-renderer#57).

establish-trade-route, before move: into any foreign city (not from a ship), or into one of the owner's own cities other than its home, 10 or more away by civ1Distance, or on another continent while that city isn't building a Wonder;

TradeRouteEstablished rules: the goods sell for ((distance + 10) * (base trade of both cities) / 24), halved on the same continent and again for your own city, and a third less for each of Railroad and Flight the destination's owner knows; added to gold and research, and unit:trade-route-established is emitted. The home city then keeps its best three routes: a route to a city it already trades with stays put (no duplicates, unlike v474.05), an empty slot is filled, or the least valuable route is replaced if the new one is worth more;
lib/baseTrade: a city's trade after corruption without its routes, with a re-entrancy guard so two cities routed to each other don't recurse.

goodsFor summed the id's characters; it now takes the base-36 counter at the end of the id, mod 8, the nearest thing to v474.05's unit slot & 7. The same-continent bonus cases register one land mass holding the world, so both cities resolve to it rather than both to null.

The trade route tests registered LandMass entries by hand, and built the World with the default registry, so the land masses it found went elsewhere. The World now gets the test's registry, and the other-continent cases build one with two Ocean columns, so the continents are the ones a game would have.

help-build-wonder is offered in your own city while it builds a Wonder, and wonder-helped adds what the Caravan cost to build (50) to the shield box. The shields stay if production changes, and any overflow is lost when the Wonder completes (civ-clone/web-renderer#57).
Registers civ1-unit's Destroyed rules and checks the Caravan is destroyed and no longer on its tile after HelpBuildWonder.

A TradeRoute is one city's route to another, held by from() and to(). Replacing one sets its to(), so it keeps its place among the city's routes. TradeRouteRegistry.getByCity() gives a city's routes in the order they were set up, and getByPartner() the routes held to it (civ-clone/web-renderer#57). Version 0.1.18.
Holds the TradeRouteRegistry, in Game and defaultGame (civ-clone/web-renderer#57). Version 0.1.8, needs core-city 0.1.18.
As the specialists slots are checked: two games don't share routes, defaultGame holds the module's TradeRouteRegistry instance, and a fresh game doesn't (civ-clone/web-renderer#57).
tradeRoutes is runtime state, and TradeRoute is a saveable class (civ-clone/web-renderer#57). Version 0.1.13.
The lock file still resolved core-city 0.1.16 and core-game 0.1.6 for the packages that range on them, so CI installed two copies of City alongside core-city 0.1.18 and the compile failed.
Re-exports the two Caravan actions from their new base-unit-action-* packages (civ-clone/web-renderer#57). Version 0.1.7.
